key_insight: SEPO improves creative generation by sampling from an optimized ensemble of system prompts, increasing diversity and novelty while trading off some quality.
engineering_relevance: Engineers can broaden a single LLM’s creative outputs at inference time without retraining by evolving and selecting behaviorally distinct system prompts.
method: Formulate creativity as multi-objective distributional optimization.
Evolve prompts and apply greedy max-min selection under a quality constraint.
Uniformly sample one selected system prompt per response.
evidence_signal: Across four tasks and three open-weight models, SEPO led 8 of 12 settings on the quality–diversity–novelty harmonic mean; average diversity rose from 1.92 to 3.43 and novelty from 1.00 to 3.34, while quality fell from 3.72 to 3.30 on LLM-judged 1–5 scales.
watch_item: The average quality decline and reliance on LLM judges warrant human validation before deployment.
paper_title: One Model, Many Modes: Evolving System Prompt Ensembles for Creative Generation
